title: Audit event actor/target confidence and retention classification
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: Define a pragmatic, forward-compatible event schema extension for audit logs that encodes actor and target attribution confidence, retention tier, and redaction guidance. This ticket focuses on: what fields to capture for actor/target attribution; a lightweight confidence score taxonomy; retention classification tags for storage/fast-path lookup; delta/diff encoding guidance for admin edits; and implementation notes for producer libraries (Go/TS) and downstream indexing.

Motivation: Existing audit events capture actor and target but lack metadata expressing uncertainty (e.g., 'service-initiated on behalf of user' vs. direct user action) and retention policy. That causes noisy alerts, storage bloat, and inconsistent search behavior. Introducing explicit confidence and retention classification will help: reduce false-positive admin alerts, allow tiered retention/cost optimizations, and provide a clear contract for downstream consumers (console, compliance exports, incident runbooks).

Scope: schema authoring, proposal for confidence taxonomy and numeric range, retention tier mapping, examples of diff encoding for policy/role edits, producer library API changes, backwards compatibility plan, rollout strategy with canaries and indexing migration. Not in scope: full storage migration (separate infra ticket) or UI redesign (console work tracked separately).
acceptance_criteria: 1) A JSON Schema and prose spec describing new top-level optional fields: actor_confidence, target_confidence, retention_tier, retention_reason, redaction_hint, and event_origin. 2) A 1-page cheat sheet mapping common events to confidence values and retention tiers. 3) Code snippets for Go/TS producer libraries showing how to populate fields, including examples for SSO/SAML-derived actors and service-on-behalf flows. 4) Backfill/migration plan for search indexes and a canary rollout checklist. 5) Security review sign-off and compatibility test plan.
notes: Design decisions considered: numeric vs. categorical confidence; we chose a small categorical set (high|medium|low|unknown) with optional normalized float [0.0-1.0] for analytics. Retention tiers align with legal/compliance buckets (ephemeral|standard|audit-7y). Redaction hints are advisory strings (e.g., 'partial-redact-email') so downstream sinks can apply deterministic redaction. Delta format recommendation uses compact field diffs (op:add/remove/replace) with context and prior_value fingerprints rather than full prior payloads to save space.
implementation_plan: 1) Finalize schema draft and JSON examples (this ticket). 2) Add fields to producer libraries and feature-flag emission. 3) Ship indexer update to understand retention_tier tags and to surface actor_confidence in search. 4) Canary for internal teams (security, infra) for 2 weeks. 5) Toggle for wider rollout and inform customers about schema extension.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Overlogging or creating a new source of PII in retention_tier/redaction_hint. Mitigation: redaction_hint must never contain raw PII; producers validate and map hints to canonical enums. Risk: Consumers assume confidence numeric meaning. Mitigation: publish clear semantics and required tests; include float only for analytics, UI should prefer categorical. Risk: storage policy misclassification leading to retention violations. Mitigation: retention_reason must reference policy IDs and require manager approval for audit-7y tier.
